title: Released TESS CPV models show no common slow egress, but crowded profiles hide short test tails
abstract: We test whether dip shapes in complex periodic variables (CPVs) have a common slow egress. We use released TESS harmonic models and compare the two half-depth intervals around each dip minimum. The main selection gives 14,606 measurements in 236 visits of 119 stars. Equal star weights give a median signed shape of -0.0071, with a 95% star bootstrap interval of -0.0176 to -0.0031. This small negative sign does not persist with all baseline, harmonic-order and window-weight choices. No tested method gives a positive median. Coefficient-space tests add one-sided exponential tails to Gaussian deficits in measured backgrounds. A 0.04-cycle positive tail gives a recovered star median of 0.0495 in crowded profiles, while a 0.01-cycle tail is largely hidden. Reflection checks confirm the direction of the estimator. The result quantifies an open visual shape question and supplies a detection test for material models. It does not exclude short tails, dust, mixed tail directions or broad profiles outside the selection. Source reduction, coefficient covariance and raw-cadence injection limits prevent a general material exclusion. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Selected star profiles have no common slow egress. The tested measurement choices and coefficient-space controls show the scope of this null result.
The test profiles lose short-tail direction after smoothing, and selection rejects some long profiles. These are effective shape tests, not a full dust model.

citations.reason: Uses its verified TESS-derived harmonic window table to measure dip direction. Does not use its drift as material motion.
The numerical source inherits its selected on-target CPV sample.
A calibrated width-depth study on the same released models motivates explicit resolution and background controls.
Section V.5 states the unresolved question of a preferred CPV dip direction.
